title: Compatibility declaration patterns and pinning guidance for open-model intake
creator: Lena Morales
description:
Problem: When teams onboard community/open models into the Redwood model catalog we have inconsistent metadata about compatibility guarantees and pinning expectations. Some entries say 'use at your own risk', others provide ad-hoc notes like 'may break streaming' or 'KV cache untested'. Lack of a consistent compatibility declaration leads to runtime failures, incorrect pin fallbacks, and excess ops work when customers surface regressions.

Goal: Define a concise, machine- and human-readable compatibility declaration pattern and a complementary pinning guidance rubric. This ticket clarifies requirements for the PRD that will be handed to engineering and docs: what metadata fields we need, validation rules, UI/console display requirements, and acceptance criteria for automated pin fallback logic.

Scope: Produce a final requirements artifact and acceptance criteria so engineering can implement: (1) a compatibility metadata schema for open models, (2) a pinning guidance rubric (when to pin, when to allow open variants), (3) validation rules and onboarding UX copy, and (4) test cases for runtime fallback behavior.
background: Historically we accepted community models with free-form notes in the catalog. As customer usage grew, several incidents occurred where unpinned model updates changed tokenization/ordering causing streaming truncation and hallucination regressions for customers on hosted endpoints. Product and runtime teams agreed we need tighter intake metadata and pinned variant fallbacks for high-risk incompatibilities. This scope should not touch curated Redwood-verified models (those already follow stricter onboarding).
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility metadata schema (JSON fields and allowed values) is defined and stored in the model catalog contract document.

Schema includes explicit fields: tokenizer_compatibility, kv_cache_compatibility, sequence_length_behavior, streaming_safety, deterministic_generation_notice, recommended_pinning_level, and minimum_test_inputs (reference prompts).
Onboarding UI validates required fields and shows structured warnings if 'recommended_pinning_level' is 'required' or 'recommended'.
Console and API surfaces the compatibility summary (human-readable) for each catalog entry and exposes the raw compatibility flags via the model metadata API.
Pinning rubric: clear rules mapping compatibility flags to pinning actions (auto-pin, recommend-pin, allow-unpinned with monitored rollout).

Runtime fallback behavior: if a serving model variant is unpinned and a compatibility regression is detected at inference time (tokenizer mismatch or decoding anomaly), requests are automatically routed to the nearest compatible pinned variant with documented audit log entries.
E2E tests: onboarding flow, metadata validation, console display, and a runtime integration test that simulates a tokenizer/kv regression and verifies fallback routing and alerting.
in_scope: Define metadata schema and allowed values for compatibility claims
Pinning guidance rubric and mapping to runtime actions
Onboarding UI validation rules and copy
API contract for exposing compatibility flags
Designs for concise console display (summary + expanded details)
out_of_scope: Retrofitting all existing catalog models (separate cleanup ticket)
Changes to curated Redwood-verified model intake (already stricter)
Runtime kernel or tokenizer engineering work (those will be separate eng tickets once requirements are accepted)
success_metrics: Reduction in catalog-related runtime incidents by 70% within 3 months of rollout
≥95% of new open-model intakes include fully populated compatibility metadata
Decreased time-to-triage for model-caused regressions (median triage time under 2 hours)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Onboarding overhead increases, causing backlog. Mitigation: provide a lightweight default 'compatibility quick-check' + templates and sample test inputs for maintainers.
Risk: Overly conservative pinning reduces access to new variants. Mitigation: include 'recommend' vs 'required' levels and allow monitored rollouts with telemetry gates.
Risk: Runtime fallback complexity introduces latency. Mitigation: require compatibility flags only for high-risk fields and validate fallback routing performance in staging before prod rollout.
ui_requirements: Console entry point should show a single-line compatibility summary (icons + brief phrase) with an expandable panel for detailed flags and test prompts. Onboarding modal should mark required fields with inline help and example prompts. API consumers should receive both the summary string and raw flags in model metadata. Copy should avoid legal/ambiguous phrasing; use explicit statements like 'Tokenization: MAY alter token indices compared toBPE v0' or 'KV cache: NOT VERIFIED for >2048 seq'.
api_contract_notes: Expose a 'compatibility' object in the model manifest (stringified in the catalog DB): keys are tokenizer_compatibility, kv_cache_compatibility, streaming_safety, sequence_length_behavior, recommended_pinning_level, test_prompts_reference. Values must be from enumerated sets. The API must also expose a compatibility_summary string generated from these flags. Engineering to propose exact enum names.
test_plan: Provide unit tests for schema validation, onboarding form tests for missing/invalid fields, and an integration test that deploys two variants (one intentionally modified tokenizer) and verifies the runtime routes traffic to pinned fallback and emits an audit event. Add monitoring alerts for 'unhandled compatibility regression' events.
rollout_plan: 1) Ship catalog schema and onboarding validation to staging with feature flag. 2) Pilot with 5 community model intakes and manual review. 3) Enable UI enforcement for new intakes only. 4) After 2 weeks of pilot telemetry, enable for all new intakes. 5) Plan a separate cleanup sprint to backfill critical existing entries. Rollout to be coordinated with runtime team and docs.
dependencies_notes: Close coordination required with Runtime (ENG kernel/tokenizer team) for defining what constitutes a tokenizer incompatibility. Also depends on Console UX for display components and Auth team for audit logging changes. Engineering tickets will be created from this PRD to implement schema, validation, and runtime fallback logic.
